subject: Cross-entity apportionment & invoice trace for AWS/GCP marketplace credits
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Hi Olga / Marcus,

We're reconciling our September marketplace billing and noticed a single credit line from "Redwood Inference" that appears to have been applied against two different legal entities on our side. Our accounting system requires us to map credits to the correct internal entity before we can book the refund. Can you provide a breakdown showing which Redwood seller entity the marketplace credited, and any tracing (invoice line references) back to the AWS/GCP metering records?

A few specifics that would help:
- Marketplace invoice ID: MP-2028-09-8671 (attached snapshot from our AP system)
- Credit amount: EUR 18,200 (single line on the invoice)
- We believe the consumption underlying the credit spans two of our projects which are billed to separate legal entities.

Please advise on your preferred format for the apportionment and whether you can include the original marketplace ledger lines (GCP/AWS) or a trace file. We need to close this by EOD Monday to meet our month-end postings.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of AP 
Avantec Ltd.
attachments: (invoice-snapshot.png)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Hi Marta — thanks for the note and the urgency. I can take this on.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
1) We'll pull the original marketplace settlement lines for the invoice you referenced (AWS and GCP) and map them to the seller entities in our system.
2) Ben will confirm the customer mapping across any contracts that could have caused a cross-entity attribution.
3) Marcus from finance will propose an apportionment journal (percent split) and provide a CSV with the trace references you can attach to your ledger.

Could you confirm which accounting entity names Avantec requires on the trace file (legal entity code vs. friendly name)? That will ensure our CSV matches your import fields.

I'll aim to get a first-pass apportionment by Monday morning. If you can share the internal purchase orders or project IDs associated with the usage, that would speed things up.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference
phone: +44 20 5555 0191

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Dec 2028 09:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Adding the mapping I have from sales/CS:
- Avantec Prod (entity code: AV-EU-P) -> Redwood seller account: RDW-EU-01
- Avantec Labs (entity code: AV-EU-L) -> Redwood seller account: RDW-EU-05

On the consumption side, the September marketplace chargeback was split across two projects (project IDs supplied to me by the account team). I do not have the raw marketplace line-item IDs in my notes, but I can pull a quick export from our sales ledger and attach.

I'll attach an internal CSV with the mapping and contract references. Marcus — can you use this to match the settlement lines and compute the percent split?

Thanks,
Ben
attachments: (entity-mapping.csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Dec 2028 08:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Thanks Ben — I pulled the settlement export from GCP and the AWS billing ledger for September. I'm seeing the single credit applied at the marketplace settlement level (internal settlement id S-2028-09-442), and the underlying usage lines show two distinct project IDs that map to the two Avantec entities Ben listed.

I've attached the annotated invoice-lines PDF showing the two consumption pools and the original settlement id references (page 2 has the ledger lines and timestamps). My recommended apportionment is:
- AV-EU-P: 62% (EUR 11,284)
- AV-EU-L: 38% (EUR 6,916)

Rationale: split by actual token/compute usage on the two project ids for the period 2028-09-01 to 2028-09-30. We captured the timestamped ledger ids so your AP team can cross-reference.

Please confirm if you want a percent-based journal or absolute EUR lines for posting. I can also produce a CSV with the marketplace invoice id, settlement id, ledger-line id, and the entity code — that should import to your ERP.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Finance Manager — Redwood Inference
attachments: (gcp-invoice-lines.pdf)

From: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Dec 2028 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Marcus / Olga — thank you for the quick turnaround and the annotated PDF. That split looks consistent with the internal usage logs we've pulled.

We prefer absolute EUR lines in the CSV so our ERP can import the exact amounts against each entity code. Attached is Avantec's required import template and our internal credit ledger extract — please populate the marketplace invoice id column and the settlement/ledger ids so the lines reconcile.

Attachments: avantec-credit-ledger.xlsx (template + ledger extract)

If you can get the completed CSV to me by EOD today we will process the refund posting this week.

Best,
Marta

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@avantec.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Dec 2028 14:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace credit on Sept invoice - request to allocate across entities

Marta — attached is the completed CSV formatted to your template with absolute EUR lines and the marketplace tracing columns populated (invoice id, settlement id, ledger_line_id). I've also uploaded the files to a shared drive and created a HubSpot ticket for audit purposes: https://hubspot.redwood.com/ticket/HD-22478 and the drive folder is https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1Qx-AP-Allocation-Avantec.

Next steps:
- Avantec to confirm import success once ERP accepts the CSV.
- Redwood finance will issue the internal journal to move the credit to the Avantec-specified entity accounts and confirm when posted (target: 48 hours).
- If Avantec needs a formal credit memo, we can produce a signed memo within 2 business days.

Thanks for the clear template — that made the reconciliation straightforward. Let us know if you want a brief call to review the trace file.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference
